summary: A thin day: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked, so every source is Hacker News. The strongest theme is that browsers still can't save or print the web properly, with five separate commenters describing garbled prints, missing exports and hand-built archives. Smaller clusters: Xcode and Rust build output eating laptop disks, tab hoarders who want a task tree instead of a flat strip, and the unsolved label-sheet mail merge.

ideas.title: Clean Print & Archive
ideas.oneLiner: One click turns any web page into a clean, paginated PDF or self-contained archive, and lets you stack several pages onto one comparison sheet.
ideas.problem: Browser print produces garbled output on many modern JS-heavy sites, and 'Save page' no longer works offline. People still rely on printing to keep order confirmations, bank payments, recipes, audit evidence and car or property listings they want to compare on paper. SaaS tools such as ticket trackers have no usable export, so people stitch screenshots together by hand.
ideas.targetUsers: Online shoppers keeping receipts and confirmations, car and property hunters comparing listings, compliance or QA staff archiving tool pages as evidence, and anyone who keeps recipes or references offline.
ideas.monetization: Free for single-page clean PDFs. Pro at about ₹149/month or ₹1,200/year adds multi-page compare sheets, evidence bundles with timestamp and URL footers, and cloud-free searchable archive folders.
mvp: Strip nav, ads, cookie banners and sticky headers with a print-specific render pass, then export to PDF
Add a footer with the page URL and capture timestamp so receipts and evidence hold up later
Queue several pages and lay them out side by side or on one sheet for comparison
Tag and store the PDFs locally with full-text search
Presets for order confirmations, bank pages, recipes and listing pages

competitors.name: SingleFile
competitors.gap: Saves a page as one HTML file, which suits power users. It doesn't produce a clean print layout, compare sheets or timestamped evidence.

competitors.name: Print Friendly & PDF
competitors.gap: Basic cleanup only. It has no multi-page comparison and no audit-style footers, and commenters say app-like pages still print badly.

competitors.name: Browser reader mode and Print to PDF
competitors.gap: Reader mode breaks on some designs, and the native print dialog is what users say produces garbage on Firefox and Chrome.

sources.title: Websites Should Be Printable
sources.quote: I used to work for a vehicle listing site, and over and over again when we talked to real users they would tell us how they would make spreadsheets and print out our vehicle pages (and from other sites too) so they could compare everything together on their kitchen table.

sources.title: Websites Should Be Printable
sources.quote: The tool is hopelessly unable to generate a sensible export or print to pdf for archiving pages to share with customers or auditors. I’ve had to resort to stitching screenshots together in MS Paint to create the offline evidence documents that I need.

sources.title: Websites Should Be Printable
sources.quote: When there is a website that I want to save indefinitely, I will print it to pdf. It means I can go back in a few years after the site is offline or has rearranged its urls (thus breaking bookmarks.)

sources.title: Websites Should Be Printable
sources.quote: It is very annoying that the print command does not work in browsers, because nowadays that is the only reliable way to save a Web page.

sources.title: Websites Should Be Printable
sources.quote: Property search websites too. Boggles my mind that Rightmove can make it possible for you to add notes on a property page but still has a shit print view.

ideas.title: Build Cruft Cleaner for Xcode & Rust
ideas.oneLiner: A small desktop app that finds Xcode DerivedData, simulators, Rust target folders and similar build output, shows what each costs, and cleans it safely.
ideas.problem: Developers on small SSDs lose tens of gigabytes to hidden build output. One Mac developer found about 8GB generated per Xcode build in a hidden folder and filled the disk over 20 releases. Another abandoned projects because Rust target directories took tens of gigabytes. Generic disk analyzers on the Mac are described as frustrating and useless for this case.
ideas.targetUsers: iOS, macOS and Rust developers on 256GB laptops or Mac minis, including indie developers who build and ship often.
ideas.monetization: Free scan, then a one-time license of about ₹1,500 (or ₹399 per year) for scheduled auto-clean, per-project rules and more ecosystems (Gradle, Flutter, node_modules, Docker).
mvp: Scan known locations: Xcode DerivedData, Archives, simulator runtimes, device support files, Rust target, node_modules, Gradle caches
Show size per project and last-built date, and list the oldest and biggest first
One-click clean with a dry-run preview and a safe-delete list that never touches source
Menu-bar nudge when free space drops below a threshold
Monthly auto-clean of projects not built in N days

competitors.name: DevCleaner for Xcode
competitors.gap: Xcode-only, so it misses Rust, Flutter and JS build output that the same developers also accumulate.

competitors.name: Kondo
competitors.gap: Command-line tool aimed at project folders. It has no scheduled cleaning or Xcode-specific caches.

competitors.name: DaisyDisk / CleanMyMac
competitors.gap: General disk analyzers. They don't know which build folders are safe to remove, and the commenter calls Apple-land analyzers useless for this.

sources.title: OBS Studio 33
sources.quote: Xcode generates a ton of hidden cruft in the DerivedData folder during every build/release that I wasn't even aware of! I spent a couple days googling and trying free & paid disk space analyzers

sources.title: 2026 is an exciting year for the Rust compiler (and me)
sources.quote: I had to abandon several projects until I bought a significantly beefier computer because of disk space, which is ridiculous. A lot of it was rust target directories taking up tens of gigabytes.

ideas.title: Research Tab Tree
ideas.oneLiner: Turns a pile of open tabs into a prunable tree per task, with notes, so research can be paused for months and resumed.
ideas.problem: People research by opening dozens of tabs in a branching pattern: wide search, shortlist, then deep dives per candidate. A flat tab strip can't show that structure. Tab hoarders keep tabs open for months, or copy links by hand into notes. ADHD users describe losing the thread and leaving ten tabs behind.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy researchers, shoppers comparing products, students doing literature reviews, and people with ADHD who start many side projects.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 trees. Pro at about ₹99/month adds unlimited trees, sync across devices, a Markdown or Obsidian export, and a 'resume where I left off' digest.
mvp: Auto-record which tab opened which, building a tree per task
Prune a branch to close or archive a whole product or topic at once
Add a one-line note to any node
Freeze a tree to a sleeping task and restore all tabs later
Export the tree to Markdown for Obsidian or Notion

competitors.name: Tree Style Tab
competitors.gap: Firefox only and a sidebar rather than a task tool. It has no notes, task freezing or export.

competitors.name: Workona
competitors.gap: Workspace-based, not a tree. Users still organize everything manually.

competitors.name: OneTab
competitors.gap: Collapses tabs into a flat list, which loses the branching structure.

sources.title: Overgrown, when plants invade your abandoned tabs
sources.quote: I wish I had another way to visualize them. A mind map would be ideal, this is also why I like tab groups and tree-style tabs.

sources.title: Overgrown, when plants invade your abandoned tabs
sources.quote: And I'm left with 10 tabs that were suppose to kick start my idea. To my own surprise I tend to go back to these ideas, but sometimes it takes me months, and sometimes, I keep these tabs on one of my devices, opened for months at a time.

ideas.title: Label Sheet Mail Merge
ideas.oneLiner: Upload a CSV, pick your adhesive label sheet, and get a PDF whose addresses line up with the labels on the first print.
ideas.problem: Mail-merging a spreadsheet onto adhesive label paper is an annual nightmare outside Microsoft Word. One user checks LibreOffice or OnlyOffice every year and ends up with misaligned labels on ruined sheets. Another commenter on the same thread suggested someone should build an app just for mail merge.
ideas.targetUsers: Small offices, clubs, nonprofits and shops that mail invoices, invitations or parcels and want an alternative to MS Word.
ideas.monetization: Free for up to 30 labels per sheet-run with a watermark. Paid at about ₹199 per month or ₹499 one-time per template pack for unlimited labels, custom sizes and saved address books.
mvp: CSV or Google Sheets import with column mapping
Built-in label presets for common sheet sizes (A4 and Letter grids)
Live preview with a margin and offset calibration test page
PDF export that stays aligned across printers
Save templates and address lists

competitors.name: Avery Design & Print
competitors.gap: Tied to Avery sheet codes and requires an account, so users on other brands still struggle with alignment.

competitors.name: LibreOffice / OnlyOffice mail merge
competitors.gap: The commenter says the process differs every year and labels still misalign despite the claimed format compatibility.

competitors.name: Microsoft Word mail merge
competitors.gap: Works but forces Windows and a Microsoft subscription, which the commenter dislikes.

sources.title: Danish Government silently drops plan to dump MS Office
sources.quote: I will try to do this same exact action, which every office in the world likely does a significant number of times per year. Every year, once I figure out how to mail merge (sometimes, a drastically different process in the interface, whereas Microsoft has kept this relatively intuitive throughout the ages) I end up with misaligned labels on a sheet of ruined label paper, despite the alleged format compatibility of the open source alternatives.

sources.title: Danish Government silently drops plan to dump MS Office
sources.quote: Maybe there should be an app just for doing mail-merge. That should be fairly simple I assume?
